topics_covered.title: 1.1 Relations, Domain and Range
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Ordered pairs, Cartesian products, coordinate graphs, domain and range algebraic determination.

• Cartesian Plane & Relations: Ordered pairs (x, y). Cartesian product A × B = {(a, b) | a ∈ A, b ∈ B}. A relation R is any subset of A × B. Domain = set of first coordinates; Range = set of second coordinates.

• Concept of Function & Vertical Line Test: A function f is a relation where EVERY domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y. Vertical Line Test: A graph represents a function if NO vertical line intersects the curve more than once.
• Linear Functions y = mx + c: Slope m = (y₂ - y₁) / (x₂ - x₁), y-intercept c. Parallel lines have equal slopes (m₁ = m₂); perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes (m₁ · m₂ = -1).

• Quadratic Functions f(x) = ax² + bx + c: Graph is a parabola. Vertex coordinates V(h, k) where h = -b/(2a) and k = f(h). Axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a). If a > 0, parabola opens upward (minimum value k); if a < 0, opens downward (maximum value k).
key_points: A relation is a function if and only if no x-value is paired with two distinct y-values.
The slope m represents rate of change: m > 0 (increasing), m < 0 (decreasing), m = 0 (horizontal line).
The vertex of a parabola (-b/(2a), f(-b/(2a))) gives the absolute maximum or minimum value.
topics_covered.explanation: Functions establish mathematical mappings where inputs generate unique outputs. Linear functions model constant rates of change, while quadratic functions model accelerated trajectories, parabolic reflectors, and cost/profit optimization curves.

topics_covered.title: 1.1 Relations, Domain and Range
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Ordered pairs, Cartesian products, coordinate graphs, domain and range algebraic determination.

• Cartesian Plane & Relations: Ordered pairs (x, y). Cartesian product A × B = {(a, b) | a ∈ A, b ∈ B}. A relation R is any subset of A × B. Domain = set of first coordinates; Range = set of second coordinates.

• Concept of Function & Vertical Line Test: A function f is a relation where EVERY domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y. Vertical Line Test: A graph represents a function if NO vertical line intersects the curve more than once.
• Linear Functions y = mx + c: Slope m = (y₂ - y₁) / (x₂ - x₁), y-intercept c. Parallel lines have equal slopes (m₁ = m₂); perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes (m₁ · m₂ = -1).

• Quadratic Functions f(x) = ax² + bx + c: Graph is a parabola. Vertex coordinates V(h, k) where h = -b/(2a) and k = f(h). Axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a). If a > 0, parabola opens upward (minimum value k); if a < 0, opens downward (maximum value k).
key_points: A relation is a function if and only if no x-value is paired with two distinct y-values.
The slope m represents rate of change: m > 0 (increasing), m < 0 (decreasing), m = 0 (horizontal line).
The vertex of a parabola (-b/(2a), f(-b/(2a))) gives the absolute maximum or minimum value.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.

worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?

topics_covered.title: 1.2 Inverse Relations and Graphical Reflection
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Reflection across line y = x, swapping coordinates, and domain/range interchange.

• Cartesian Plane & Relations: Ordered pairs (x, y). Cartesian product A × B = {(a, b) | a ∈ A, b ∈ B}. A relation R is any subset of A × B. Domain = set of first coordinates; Range = set of second coordinates.

• Concept of Function & Vertical Line Test: A function f is a relation where EVERY domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y. Vertical Line Test: A graph represents a function if NO vertical line intersects the curve more than once.
• Linear Functions y = mx + c: Slope m = (y₂ - y₁) / (x₂ - x₁), y-intercept c. Parallel lines have equal slopes (m₁ = m₂); perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes (m₁ · m₂ = -1).

• Quadratic Functions f(x) = ax² + bx + c: Graph is a parabola. Vertex coordinates V(h, k) where h = -b/(2a) and k = f(h). Axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a). If a > 0, parabola opens upward (minimum value k); if a < 0, opens downward (maximum value k).
key_points: A relation is a function if and only if no x-value is paired with two distinct y-values.
The slope m represents rate of change: m > 0 (increasing), m < 0 (decreasing), m = 0 (horizontal line).
The vertex of a parabola (-b/(2a), f(-b/(2a))) gives the absolute maximum or minimum value.

core_formulas_rules.explanation: Calculates Euclidean distance and midpoint coordinates in the 2D Cartesian coordinate plane.
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Applies to any points A(x₁, y₁) and B(x₂, y₂).

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 1.4 Composition of Functions
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Composite function (f o g)(x) = f(g(x)), domain restrictions of composite functions, and non-commutativity.

• Cartesian Plane & Relations: Ordered pairs (x, y). Cartesian product A × B = {(a, b) | a ∈ A, b ∈ B}. A relation R is any subset of A × B. Domain = set of first coordinates; Range = set of second coordinates.

• Concept of Function & Vertical Line Test: A function f is a relation where EVERY domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y. Vertical Line Test: A graph represents a function if NO vertical line intersects the curve more than once.
• Linear Functions y = mx + c: Slope m = (y₂ - y₁) / (x₂ - x₁), y-intercept c. Parallel lines have equal slopes (m₁ = m₂); perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes (m₁ · m₂ = -1).

• Quadratic Functions f(x) = ax² + bx + c: Graph is a parabola. Vertex coordinates V(h, k) where h = -b/(2a) and k = f(h). Axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a). If a > 0, parabola opens upward (minimum value k); if a < 0, opens downward (maximum value k).
key_points: A relation is a function if and only if no x-value is paired with two distinct y-values.
The slope m represents rate of change: m > 0 (increasing), m < 0 (decreasing), m = 0 (horizontal line).
The vertex of a parabola (-b/(2a), f(-b/(2a))) gives the absolute maximum or minimum value.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 1.5 Inverse Functions and Their Graphs
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Condition for invertibility (bijectivity), finding algebraic formula for f^-1(x), and graphical symmetry.

• Cartesian Plane & Relations: Ordered pairs (x, y). Cartesian product A × B = {(a, b) | a ∈ A, b ∈ B}. A relation R is any subset of A × B. Domain = set of first coordinates; Range = set of second coordinates.

• Concept of Function & Vertical Line Test: A function f is a relation where EVERY domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y. Vertical Line Test: A graph represents a function if NO vertical line intersects the curve more than once.
• Linear Functions y = mx + c: Slope m = (y₂ - y₁) / (x₂ - x₁), y-intercept c. Parallel lines have equal slopes (m₁ = m₂); perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes (m₁ · m₂ = -1).

• Quadratic Functions f(x) = ax² + bx + c: Graph is a parabola. Vertex coordinates V(h, k) where h = -b/(2a) and k = f(h). Axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a). If a > 0, parabola opens upward (minimum value k); if a < 0, opens downward (maximum value k).
key_points: A relation is a function if and only if no x-value is paired with two distinct y-values.
The slope m represents rate of change: m > 0 (increasing), m < 0 (decreasing), m = 0 (horizontal line).
The vertex of a parabola (-b/(2a), f(-b/(2a))) gives the absolute maximum or minimum value.

• Cartesian Plane & Relations: Ordered pairs (x, y). Cartesian product A × B = {(a, b) | a ∈ A, b ∈ B}. A relation R is any subset of A × B. Domain = set of first coordinates; Range = set of second coordinates.

• Concept of Function & Vertical Line Test: A function f is a relation where EVERY domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y. Vertical Line Test: A graph represents a function if NO vertical line intersects the curve more than once.
• Linear Functions y = mx + c: Slope m = (y₂ - y₁) / (x₂ - x₁), y-intercept c. Parallel lines have equal slopes (m₁ = m₂); perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes (m₁ · m₂ = -1).

• Quadratic Functions f(x) = ax² + bx + c: Graph is a parabola. Vertex coordinates V(h, k) where h = -b/(2a) and k = f(h). Axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a). If a > 0, parabola opens upward (minimum value k); if a < 0, opens downward (maximum value k).
key_points: A relation is a function if and only if no x-value is paired with two distinct y-values.
The slope m represents rate of change: m > 0 (increasing), m < 0 (decreasing), m = 0 (horizontal line).
The vertex of a parabola (-b/(2a), f(-b/(2a))) gives the absolute maximum or minimum value.

core_formulas_rules.formula_or_law: Quadratic Formula & Nature of Roots: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a)
core_formulas_rules.explanation: Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac dictates root characteristics: Δ > 0 (two distinct real roots), Δ = 0 (repeated real root), Δ < 0 (complex conjugate roots).
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Valid for any quadratic equation in canonical form ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0.

core_formulas_rules.formula_or_law: Vieta's Formulas: Sum of roots = -b/a, Product of roots = c/a
core_formulas_rules.explanation: Enables rapid verification of roots and construction of quadratic polynomials without lengthy factoring.
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Applicable to any degree-2 polynomial with real or complex coefficients.

core_formulas_rules.formula_or_law: Distance & Midpoint: d = √[(x₂ - x₁)² + (y₂ - y₁)²], M = ((x₁+x₂)/2, (y₁+y₂)/2)
core_formulas_rules.explanation: Calculates Euclidean distance and midpoint coordinates in the 2D Cartesian coordinate plane.
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Applies to any points A(x₁, y₁) and B(x₂, y₂).

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Horizontal line test, one-to-one (injective), onto (surjective), bijective mappings, and signum/step functions.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: A relation is a function if and only if no x-value is paired with two distinct y-values.
- **The slope m represents rate of change**: The slope m represents rate of change: m > 0 (increasing), m < 0 (decreasing), m = 0 (horizontal line).
- **Key Principle**: The vertex of a parabola (-b/(2a), f(-b/(2a))) gives the absolute maximum or minimum value.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Parabola Vertex Geometry: Parabola y = ax² + bx + c ──> Axis of Symmetry Line x = -b/(2a) ──> Vertex Point V(-b/(2a), k) [Max if a < 0, Min if a > 0].
```

topics_covered.title: 1.4 Composition of Functions
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Composite function (f o g)(x) = f(g(x)), domain restrictions of composite functions, and non-commutativity.

• Cartesian Plane & Relations: Ordered pairs (x, y). Cartesian product A × B = {(a, b) | a ∈ A, b ∈ B}. A relation R is any subset of A × B. Domain = set of first coordinates; Range = set of second coordinates.

• Concept of Function & Vertical Line Test: A function f is a relation where EVERY domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y. Vertical Line Test: A graph represents a function if NO vertical line intersects the curve more than once.
• Linear Functions y = mx + c: Slope m = (y₂ - y₁) / (x₂ - x₁), y-intercept c. Parallel lines have equal slopes (m₁ = m₂); perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes (m₁ · m₂ = -1).

• Quadratic Functions f(x) = ax² + bx + c: Graph is a parabola. Vertex coordinates V(h, k) where h = -b/(2a) and k = f(h). Axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a). If a > 0, parabola opens upward (minimum value k); if a < 0, opens downward (maximum value k).
key_points: A relation is a function if and only if no x-value is paired with two distinct y-values.
The slope m represents rate of change: m > 0 (increasing), m < 0 (decreasing), m = 0 (horizontal line).
The vertex of a parabola (-b/(2a), f(-b/(2a))) gives the absolute maximum or minimum value.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example 1: 1.1 Relations, Domain and Range
worked_examples.problem: Analyze and apply the governing curriculum principles of 1.1 Relations, Domain and Range (Relations and Functions).
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: A relation is a function if and only if no x-value is paired with two distinct y-values.
Step 2: The slope m represents rate of change: m > 0 (increasing), m < 0 (decreasing), m = 0 (horizontal line).
Step 3: The vertex of a parabola (-b/(2a), f(-b/(2a))) gives the absolute maximum or minimum value.
worked_examples.result: Functions pass the Vertical Line Test; linear slope is m = Δy/Δx, and parabolic vertex occurs at x = -b/(2a).
worked_examples.examiner_note: Frequent EUEE questions: evaluating f(x) at given values, finding the vertex of f(x) = 2x² - 8x + 5, finding slope of perpendicular lines, and determining function domain.

topics_covered.title: 2.1 Rational Expressions: Simplification and Operations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Simplification, domain exclusions, addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of polynomial fractions.

• Cartesian Plane & Relations: Ordered pairs (x, y). Cartesian product A × B = {(a, b) | a ∈ A, b ∈ B}. A relation R is any subset of A × B. Domain = set of first coordinates; Range = set of second coordinates.

• Concept of Function & Vertical Line Test: A function f is a relation where EVERY domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y. Vertical Line Test: A graph represents a function if NO vertical line intersects the curve more than once.
• Linear Functions y = mx + c: Slope m = (y₂ - y₁) / (x₂ - x₁), y-intercept c. Parallel lines have equal slopes (m₁ = m₂); perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes (m₁ · m₂ = -1).

• Quadratic Functions f(x) = ax² + bx + c: Graph is a parabola. Vertex coordinates V(h, k) where h = -b/(2a) and k = f(h). Axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a). If a > 0, parabola opens upward (minimum value k); if a < 0, opens downward (maximum value k).
key_points: A relation is a function if and only if no x-value is paired with two distinct y-values.
The slope m represents rate of change: m > 0 (increasing), m < 0 (decreasing), m = 0 (horizontal line).
The vertex of a parabola (-b/(2a), f(-b/(2a))) gives the absolute maximum or minimum value.
topics_covered.explanation: Functions establish mathematical mappings where inputs generate unique outputs. Linear functions model constant rates of change, while quadratic functions model accelerated trajectories, parabolic reflectors, and cost/profit optimization curves.
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: Functions establish mathematical mappings where inputs generate unique outputs. Linear functions model constant rates of change, while quadratic functions model accelerated trajectories, parabolic reflectors, and cost/profit optimization curves.

topics_covered.title: 2.1 Rational Expressions: Simplification and Operations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Simplification, domain exclusions, addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of polynomial fractions.
• Number System Hierarchy: ℕ (Natural) ⊂ 𝕎 (Whole) ⊂ ℤ (Integers) ⊂ ℚ (Rationals) ⊂ ℝ (Real Numbers). Complex numbers ℂ contain all real and imaginary roots.

• Rational vs. Irrational Numbers: Rational numbers can be written as a/b (b ≠ 0) with terminating or repeating decimals. Irrational numbers cannot be expressed as a fraction and have non-terminating, non-repeating decimals (e.g. √2, π, e).
• Proof of Irrationality of √2: By contradiction: assume √2 = a/b in lowest terms. 2b² = a² ⇒ a is even ⇒ 4k² = 2b² ⇒ b is even. Contradicts assumption of lowest terms.
• Radical Algebraic Rules: √(ab) = √a·√b and √(a/b) = √a/√b for a, b ≥ 0. Rationalizing denominators: multiply by conjugate (√a - √b) / (√a - √b) to eliminate surds from denominator.
• Absolute Value Properties: |x| = x if x ≥ 0, and -x if x < 0. Triangle inequality: |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|. Distance between points a and b is |a - b|.
key_points: Between any two distinct rational numbers, there are infinitely many rational and irrational numbers (dense property of ℝ).
√x² = |x|, NOT simply x. If x is negative, √((-3)²) = |-3| = 3.
Never cancel across addition inside a radical: √(a² + b²) ≠ a + b.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 2.2 Rational Equations and Rational Inequalities
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Clearing denominators, extraneous solutions, sign tables (critical value intervals) for solving inequalities.
• Number System Hierarchy: ℕ (Natural) ⊂ 𝕎 (Whole) ⊂ ℤ (Integers) ⊂ ℚ (Rationals) ⊂ ℝ (Real Numbers). Complex numbers ℂ contain all real and imaginary roots.

• Rational vs. Irrational Numbers: Rational numbers can be written as a/b (b ≠ 0) with terminating or repeating decimals. Irrational numbers cannot be expressed as a fraction and have non-terminating, non-repeating decimals (e.g. √2, π, e).
• Proof of Irrationality of √2: By contradiction: assume √2 = a/b in lowest terms. 2b² = a² ⇒ a is even ⇒ 4k² = 2b² ⇒ b is even. Contradicts assumption of lowest terms.
• Radical Algebraic Rules: √(ab) = √a·√b and √(a/b) = √a/√b for a, b ≥ 0. Rationalizing denominators: multiply by conjugate (√a - √b) / (√a - √b) to eliminate surds from denominator.
• Absolute Value Properties: |x| = x if x ≥ 0, and -x if x < 0. Triangle inequality: |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|. Distance between points a and b is |a - b|.
key_points: Between any two distinct rational numbers, there are infinitely many rational and irrational numbers (dense property of ℝ).
√x² = |x|, NOT simply x. If x is negative, √((-3)²) = |-3| = 3.
Never cancel across addition inside a radical: √(a² + b²) ≠ a + b.

Linear functions model constant rates of change, while quadratic functions model accelerated trajectories, parabolic reflectors, and cost/profit optimization curves.

topics_covered.title: 2.3 Rational Functions, Asymptotes and Graphs
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Vertical asymptotes, horizontal asymptotes, oblique (slant) asymptotes, holes (removable discontinuities), and intercepts.

• Cartesian Plane & Relations: Ordered pairs (x, y). Cartesian product A × B = {(a, b) | a ∈ A, b ∈ B}. A relation R is any subset of A × B. Domain = set of first coordinates; Range = set of second coordinates.

• Concept of Function & Vertical Line Test: A function f is a relation where EVERY domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y. Vertical Line Test: A graph represents a function if NO vertical line intersects the curve more than once.
• Linear Functions y = mx + c: Slope m = (y₂ - y₁) / (x₂ - x₁), y-intercept c. Parallel lines have equal slopes (m₁ = m₂); perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes (m₁ · m₂ = -1).

• Quadratic Functions f(x) = ax² + bx + c: Graph is a parabola. Vertex coordinates V(h, k) where h = -b/(2a) and k = f(h). Axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a). If a > 0, parabola opens upward (minimum value k); if a < 0, opens downward (maximum value k).
key_points: A relation is a function if and only if no x-value is paired with two distinct y-values.
The slope m represents rate of change: m > 0 (increasing), m < 0 (decreasing), m = 0 (horizontal line).
The vertex of a parabola (-b/(2a), f(-b/(2a))) gives the absolute maximum or minimum value.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 2.1 Rational Expressions: Simplification and Operations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Simplification, domain exclusions, addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of polynomial fractions.

• Cartesian Plane & Relations: Ordered pairs (x, y). Cartesian product A × B = {(a, b) | a ∈ A, b ∈ B}. A relation R is any subset of A × B. Domain = set of first coordinates; Range = set of second coordinates.

• Concept of Function & Vertical Line Test: A function f is a relation where EVERY domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y. Vertical Line Test: A graph represents a function if NO vertical line intersects the curve more than once.
• Linear Functions y = mx + c: Slope m = (y₂ - y₁) / (x₂ - x₁), y-intercept c. Parallel lines have equal slopes (m₁ = m₂); perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes (m₁ · m₂ = -1).

• Quadratic Functions f(x) = ax² + bx + c: Graph is a parabola. Vertex coordinates V(h, k) where h = -b/(2a) and k = f(h). Axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a). If a > 0, parabola opens upward (minimum value k); if a < 0, opens downward (maximum value k).
key_points: A relation is a function if and only if no x-value is paired with two distinct y-values.
The slope m represents rate of change: m > 0 (increasing), m < 0 (decreasing), m = 0 (horizontal line).
The vertex of a parabola (-b/(2a), f(-b/(2a))) gives the absolute maximum or minimum value.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Functions establish mathematical mappings where inputs generate unique outputs. Linear functions model constant rates of change, while quadratic functions model accelerated trajectories, parabolic reflectors, and cost/profit optimization curves.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Simplification, domain exclusions, addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of polynomial fractions.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: A relation is a function if and only if no x-value is paired with two distinct y-values.
- **The slope m represents rate of change**: The slope m represents rate of change: m > 0 (increasing), m < 0 (decreasing), m = 0 (horizontal line).
- **Key Principle**: The vertex of a parabola (-b/(2a), f(-b/(2a))) gives the absolute maximum or minimum value.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Parabola Vertex Geometry: Parabola y = ax² + bx + c ──> Axis of Symmetry Line x = -b/(2a) ──> Vertex Point V(-b/(2a), k) [Max if a < 0, Min if a > 0].
```

topics_covered.title: 3.1 Concepts of a Matrix and Matrix Notations
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.1 Concepts of a Matrix and Matrix Notations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Dimensions (rows x columns), entries, row vectors, column vectors, square matrices, and equality of matrices.

• Scalars vs Vectors: Scalar quantity has magnitude only (mass, temperature, speed, energy). Vector quantity has BOTH magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force, acceleration). Directed line segment representation AB.

• 2D Vector Component Form: Vector v in Cartesian plane: v = (v_x, v_y) = v_x i + v_y j, where i = (1, 0) and j = (0, 1) are standard unit vectors along x and y axes. Components: v_x = ||v|| cos θ, v_y = ||v|| sin θ.
• Magnitude & Direction Angle: Magnitude ||v|| = √(v_x² + v_y²). Direction angle θ = tan⁻¹(v_y / v_x) (quadrant adjusted). Unit vector u in direction of v: u = v / ||v||.

• Vector Operations: Vector addition u + v = (u_x + v_x, u_y + v_y) (Triangle / Parallelogram Law). Scalar multiplication k·v = (k·v_x, k·v_y). Dot product u · v = u_x v_x + u_y v_y = ||u|| ||v|| cos θ.
key_points: Magnitude of a vector is always a non-negative scalar ||v|| ≥ 0.
A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1: ||u|| = 1.
Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero: u · v = 0.
topics_covered.explanation: Vectors represent directional physical quantities. Decomposing vectors into orthogonal x and y components transforms complex 2D vector addition into simple scalar arithmetic along independent coordinate axes.

topics_covered.title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Augmented matrices, consistent vs. inconsistent systems, unique solutions, infinitely many solutions, and geometric interpretation.

• Linear Equations & Inequalities in 1 Variable: Form ax + b = 0 (solution x = -b/a). Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number REVERSES the inequality sign (e.g., -2x < 6 ⟹ x > -3). Solution sets expressed on real line or in interval notation.

• Systems of 2-Variable Linear Equations: ax + by = c and dx + ey = f. Solution methods: 1) Substitution; 2) Elimination; 3) Graphical intersection point (x, y). Consistent unique solution (intersecting lines), inconsistent no solution (parallel lines), dependent infinite solutions (coincident lines).
• Quadratic Equations: Standard form ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0). Methods: Factoring, completing the square, and Quadratic Formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a).
• Discriminant Analysis (Δ = b² - 4ac): If Δ > 0, two distinct real roots; If Δ = 0, one real repeated root (x = -b/(2a)); If Δ < 0, two complex conjugate roots (no real roots).
key_points: Reversing the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number is mandatory.
Extraneous roots must be checked whenever denominators contain variables.
Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac instantly reveals the number and nature of quadratic roots without full solving.
topics_covered.explanation: Algebraic equations and inequalities model balanced quantities and constraints. Linear systems resolve simultaneous conditions, while quadratic equations analyze parabolic trajectories and maximum/minimum optimization problems.
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: Algebraic equations and inequalities model balanced quantities and constraints. Linear systems resolve simultaneous conditions, while quadratic equations analyze parabolic trajectories and maximum/minimum optimization problems.

topics_covered.topic_title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Invertibility condition, Gauss-Jordan elimination [A | I] -> [I | A^-1], and solving AX = B via X = A^-1 B.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Input-output Leontief economic models, network communication graphs, inventory tracking, and cryptography.
• Data Organization & Frequency Distributions: Discrete vs grouped frequency tables. Class intervals, lower/upper class boundaries, class mark (midpoint x = (L + U)/2), and cumulative frequency.

• Graphical Data Representations: Bar charts (discrete categories, gaps between bars); Histograms (continuous data, bars touch, bar area proportional to frequency); Pie charts (circular sectors, sector angle = (f / N) × 360°).

• Measures of Central Tendency: 1) Mean x̄ = (Σ x) / n or x̄ = (Σ f·x) / (Σ f); 2) Median: Middle score when data is ordered (for even n, average of two middle terms); 3) Mode: Most frequently occurring score (unimodal, bimodal, or no mode).
• Basic Probability Concepts: Sample space S (all possible outcomes), Event E (subset of S). Theoretical Probability P(E) = n(E) / n(S) where 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1. Complementary Event: P(E') = 1 - P(E).
key_points: In a histogram, bars MUST touch because data is continuous; in a bar chart, gaps separate discrete categories.
The sum of sector angles in a pie chart is ALWAYS 360°.
Probability is strictly bounded: 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1 (0 = impossible event, 1 = certain event).
topics_covered.explanation: Statistics and probability provide tools for analyzing data and quantifying uncertainty. Descriptive statistics condense large data sets into summary averages and charts, while probability models chance events.

short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Dimensions (rows x columns), entries, row vectors, column vectors, square matrices, and equality of matrices.

• Scalars vs Vectors: Scalar quantity has magnitude only (mass, temperature, speed, energy). Vector quantity has BOTH magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force, acceleration). Directed line segment representation AB.

• 2D Vector Component Form: Vector v in Cartesian plane: v = (v_x, v_y) = v_x i + v_y j, where i = (1, 0) and j = (0, 1) are standard unit vectors along x and y axes. Components: v_x = ||v|| cos θ, v_y = ||v|| sin θ.
• Magnitude & Direction Angle: Magnitude ||v|| = √(v_x² + v_y²). Direction angle θ = tan⁻¹(v_y / v_x) (quadrant adjusted). Unit vector u in direction of v: u = v / ||v||.

• Vector Operations: Vector addition u + v = (u_x + v_x, u_y + v_y) (Triangle / Parallelogram Law). Scalar multiplication k·v = (k·v_x, k·v_y). Dot product u · v = u_x v_x + u_y v_y = ||u|| ||v|| cos θ.
key_points: Magnitude of a vector is always a non-negative scalar ||v|| ≥ 0.
A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1: ||u|| = 1.
Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero: u · v = 0.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

quick_example.step_solution:

Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?

• Scalars vs Vectors: Scalar quantity has magnitude only (mass, temperature, speed, energy). Vector quantity has BOTH magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force, acceleration). Directed line segment representation AB.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

book-11-soc-math_ch_3_topic_3_4_elementa.detailed_overview: Vectors represent directional physical quantities. Decomposing vectors into orthogonal x and y components transforms complex 2D vector addition into simple scalar arithmetic along independent coordinate axes.

topics_covered.title: 3.4 Elementary Row Operations and Gaussian Elimination
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.4 Elementary Row Operations and Gaussian Elimination
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Row swapping, scalar multiplication of rows, row replacement, and reducing to row-echelon form.

• Scalars vs Vectors: Scalar quantity has magnitude only (mass, temperature, speed, energy). Vector quantity has BOTH magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force, acceleration). Directed line segment representation AB.

• 2D Vector Component Form: Vector v in Cartesian plane: v = (v_x, v_y) = v_x i + v_y j, where i = (1, 0) and j = (0, 1) are standard unit vectors along x and y axes. Components: v_x = ||v|| cos θ, v_y = ||v|| sin θ.
• Magnitude & Direction Angle: Magnitude ||v|| = √(v_x² + v_y²). Direction angle θ = tan⁻¹(v_y / v_x) (quadrant adjusted). Unit vector u in direction of v: u = v / ||v||.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Augmented matrices, consistent vs. inconsistent systems, unique solutions, infinitely many solutions, and geometric interpretation.

• Linear Equations & Inequalities in 1 Variable: Form ax + b = 0 (solution x = -b/a). Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number REVERSES the inequality sign (e.g., -2x < 6 ⟹ x > -3). Solution sets expressed on real line or in interval notation.

• Systems of 2-Variable Linear Equations: ax + by = c and dx + ey = f. Solution methods: 1) Substitution; 2) Elimination; 3) Graphical intersection point (x, y). Consistent unique solution (intersecting lines), inconsistent no solution (parallel lines), dependent infinite solutions (coincident lines).
• Quadratic Equations: Standard form ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0). Methods: Factoring, completing the square, and Quadratic Formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a).
• Discriminant Analysis (Δ = b² - 4ac): If Δ > 0, two distinct real roots; If Δ = 0, one real repeated root (x = -b/(2a)); If Δ < 0, two complex conjugate roots (no real roots).
key_points: Reversing the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number is mandatory.
Extraneous roots must be checked whenever denominators contain variables.
Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac instantly reveals the number and nature of quadratic roots without full solving.

topics_covered.topic_title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Augmented matrices, consistent vs. inconsistent systems, unique solutions, infinitely many solutions, and geometric interpretation.

• Linear Equations & Inequalities in 1 Variable: Form ax + b = 0 (solution x = -b/a). Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number REVERSES the inequality sign (e.g., -2x < 6 ⟹ x > -3). Solution sets expressed on real line or in interval notation.

• Systems of 2-Variable Linear Equations: ax + by = c and dx + ey = f. Solution methods: 1) Substitution; 2) Elimination; 3) Graphical intersection point (x, y). Consistent unique solution (intersecting lines), inconsistent no solution (parallel lines), dependent infinite solutions (coincident lines).
• Quadratic Equations: Standard form ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0). Methods: Factoring, completing the square, and Quadratic Formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a).
• Discriminant Analysis (Δ = b² - 4ac): If Δ > 0, two distinct real roots; If Δ = 0, one real repeated root (x = -b/(2a)); If Δ < 0, two complex conjugate roots (no real roots).
key_points: Reversing the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number is mandatory.
Extraneous roots must be checked whenever denominators contain variables.
Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac instantly reveals the number and nature of quadratic roots without full solving.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

topics_covered.title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Invertibility condition, Gauss-Jordan elimination [A | I] -> [I | A^-1], and solving AX = B via X = A^-1 B.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).
topics_covered.explanation: Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.

quick_example.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
quick_example.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 3.1 Concepts of a Matrix and Matrix Notations
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.1 Concepts of a Matrix and Matrix Notations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Dimensions (rows x columns), entries, row vectors, column vectors, square matrices, and equality of matrices.

• Scalars vs Vectors: Scalar quantity has magnitude only (mass, temperature, speed, energy). Vector quantity has BOTH magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force, acceleration). Directed line segment representation AB.

• 2D Vector Component Form: Vector v in Cartesian plane: v = (v_x, v_y) = v_x i + v_y j, where i = (1, 0) and j = (0, 1) are standard unit vectors along x and y axes. Components: v_x = ||v|| cos θ, v_y = ||v|| sin θ.
• Magnitude & Direction Angle: Magnitude ||v|| = √(v_x² + v_y²). Direction angle θ = tan⁻¹(v_y / v_x) (quadrant adjusted). Unit vector u in direction of v: u = v / ||v||.

• Vector Operations: Vector addition u + v = (u_x + v_x, u_y + v_y) (Triangle / Parallelogram Law). Scalar multiplication k·v = (k·v_x, k·v_y). Dot product u · v = u_x v_x + u_y v_y = ||u|| ||v|| cos θ.
key_points: Magnitude of a vector is always a non-negative scalar ||v|| ≥ 0.
A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1: ||u|| = 1.
Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero: u · v = 0.
topics_covered.explanation:
### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Vectors represent directional physical quantities. Decomposing vectors into orthogonal x and y components transforms complex 2D vector addition into simple scalar arithmetic along independent coordinate axes.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Dimensions (rows x columns), entries, row vectors, column vectors, square matrices, and equality of matrices.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: Magnitude of a vector is always a non-negative scalar ||v|| ≥ 0.
- **A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1**: A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1: ||u|| = 1.
- **Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero**: Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero: u · v = 0.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema

topics_covered.title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Augmented matrices, consistent vs. inconsistent systems, unique solutions, infinitely many solutions, and geometric interpretation.

• Linear Equations & Inequalities in 1 Variable: Form ax + b = 0 (solution x = -b/a). Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number REVERSES the inequality sign (e.g., -2x < 6 ⟹ x > -3). Solution sets expressed on real line or in interval notation.

• Systems of 2-Variable Linear Equations: ax + by = c and dx + ey = f. Solution methods: 1) Substitution; 2) Elimination; 3) Graphical intersection point (x, y). Consistent unique solution (intersecting lines), inconsistent no solution (parallel lines), dependent infinite solutions (coincident lines).
• Quadratic Equations: Standard form ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0). Methods: Factoring, completing the square, and Quadratic Formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a).
• Discriminant Analysis (Δ = b² - 4ac): If Δ > 0, two distinct real roots; If Δ = 0, one real repeated root (x = -b/(2a)); If Δ < 0, two complex conjugate roots (no real roots).
key_points: Reversing the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number is mandatory.
Extraneous roots must be checked whenever denominators contain variables.
Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac instantly reveals the number and nature of quadratic roots without full solving.

Algebraic equations and inequalities model balanced quantities and constraints. Linear systems resolve simultaneous conditions, while quadratic equations analyze parabolic trajectories and maximum/minimum optimization problems.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Augmented matrices, consistent vs. inconsistent systems, unique solutions, infinitely many solutions, and geometric interpretation.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: Reversing the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number is mandatory.
- **Key Principle**: Extraneous roots must be checked whenever denominators contain variables.
- **Key Principle**: Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac instantly reveals the number and nature of quadratic roots without full solving.

```text
Quadratic Discriminant Curve: Δ > 0 (Parabola crosses x-axis twice) ──> Δ = 0 (Parabola touches x-axis at vertex) ──> Δ < 0 (Parabola floats above/below x-axis).
```

topics_covered.title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Invertibility condition, Gauss-Jordan elimination [A | I] -> [I | A^-1], and solving AX = B via X = A^-1 B.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Invertibility condition, Gauss-Jordan elimination [A | I] -> [I | A^-1], and solving AX = B via X = A^-1 B.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **To find the inverse algebraically**: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
- **Key Principle**: f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
- **Key Principle**: A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

**Visual / Experimental Schema:**

```text
Function Mapping Machine: Input x ──> [Function f(x)] ──> Output y ──> [Inverse Function f⁻¹(y)] ──> Returns original x.
```

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Economic demand-supply equilibrium models and commodity pricing curves in Ethiopia's ECX (Ethiopian Commodity Exchange) are modeled as inverse functions.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors

topics_covered.title: 3.7 Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.7 Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Input-output Leontief economic models, network communication graphs, inventory tracking, and cryptography.
• Data Organization & Frequency Distributions: Discrete vs grouped frequency tables. Class intervals, lower/upper class boundaries, class mark (midpoint x = (L + U)/2), and cumulative frequency.

• Graphical Data Representations: Bar charts (discrete categories, gaps between bars); Histograms (continuous data, bars touch, bar area proportional to frequency); Pie charts (circular sectors, sector angle = (f / N) × 360°).

• Measures of Central Tendency: 1) Mean x̄ = (Σ x) / n or x̄ = (Σ f·x) / (Σ f); 2) Median: Middle score when data is ordered (for even n, average of two middle terms); 3) Mode: Most frequently occurring score (unimodal, bimodal, or no mode).
• Basic Probability Concepts: Sample space S (all possible outcomes), Event E (subset of S). Theoretical Probability P(E) = n(E) / n(S) where 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1. Complementary Event: P(E') = 1 - P(E).
key_points: In a histogram, bars MUST touch because data is continuous; in a bar chart, gaps separate discrete categories.
The sum of sector angles in a pie chart is ALWAYS 360°.
Probability is strictly bounded: 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1 (0 = impossible event, 1 = certain event).
topics_covered.explanation:
### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Statistics and probability provide tools for analyzing data and quantifying uncertainty. Descriptive statistics condense large data sets into summary averages and charts, while probability models chance events.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Input-output Leontief economic models, network communication graphs, inventory tracking, and cryptography.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: In a histogram, bars MUST touch because data is continuous; in a bar chart, gaps separate discrete categories.
- **Key Principle**: The sum of sector angles in a pie chart is ALWAYS 360°.
- **Probability is strictly bounded**: Probability is strictly bounded: 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1 (0 = impossible event, 1 = certain event).

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Data Central Tendency Distributions: Symmetric Distribution (Mean = Median = Mode) ──> Positively Skewed (Mode < Median < Mean) ──> Negatively Skewed (Mean < Median < Mode).
```


| Parameter / Aspect | Academic Specification & Meaning | National Syllabus Standard |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Core Topic** | 3.7 Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business | Unit 3 Framework |
| **Governing Law** | Mean x̄ = Σ(f·x)/N; Median is middle value; Mode is most frequent; Probability P... | Formulated per MoE Guidelines |
| **Examination Traps** | High-frequency EUEE questions: calculating mean of grouped frequency data, calcu... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Agricultural crop yield forecasting and national health epidemic tracking by the Ethiopian Public Health Institute rely on statistical measures and probability models.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors
High-frequency EUEE questions: calculating mean of grouped frequency data, calculating pie chart sector angles, finding median from cumulative frequency, and calculating basic event probabilities.

### 6. Comprehensive Student Takeaway
Mean x̄ = Σ(f·x)/N; Median is middle value; Mode is most frequent; Probability P(E) = n(E)/n(S) where 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example 1: 3.1 Concepts of a Matrix and Matrix Notations
worked_examples.problem: Analyze and apply the governing curriculum principles of 3.1 Concepts of a Matrix and Matrix Notations (Matrices).
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Magnitude of a vector is always a non-negative scalar ||v|| ≥ 0.
Step 2: A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1: ||u|| = 1.
Step 3: Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero: u · v = 0.

topics_covered.title: 4.1 Determinants of 2x2 Matrices
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Formula det(A) = ad - bc, geometric interpretation as signed area of parallelogram formed by row vectors.

• Scalars vs Vectors: Scalar quantity has magnitude only (mass, temperature, speed, energy). Vector quantity has BOTH magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force, acceleration). Directed line segment representation AB.

• 2D Vector Component Form: Vector v in Cartesian plane: v = (v_x, v_y) = v_x i + v_y j, where i = (1, 0) and j = (0, 1) are standard unit vectors along x and y axes. Components: v_x = ||v|| cos θ, v_y = ||v|| sin θ.
• Magnitude & Direction Angle: Magnitude ||v|| = √(v_x² + v_y²). Direction angle θ = tan⁻¹(v_y / v_x) (quadrant adjusted). Unit vector u in direction of v: u = v / ||v||.

• Vector Operations: Vector addition u + v = (u_x + v_x, u_y + v_y) (Triangle / Parallelogram Law). Scalar multiplication k·v = (k·v_x, k·v_y). Dot product u · v = u_x v_x + u_y v_y = ||u|| ||v|| cos θ.
key_points: Magnitude of a vector is always a non-negative scalar ||v|| ≥ 0.
A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1: ||u|| = 1.
Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero: u · v = 0.
topics_covered.explanation: Vectors represent directional physical quantities. Decomposing vectors into orthogonal x and y components transforms complex 2D vector addition into simple scalar arithmetic along independent coordinate axes.
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: Vectors represent directional physical quantities. Decomposing vectors into orthogonal x and y components transforms complex 2D vector addition into simple scalar arithmetic along independent coordinate axes.
